Corrected. The article governs a substantival adjective, so the supplied generic noun ones is the article's own (rules 17, 102): rule 17's generic-noun clause is scoped in terms to anarthrous Greek, and here a Greek article stands to take it. The demonstrative these displaces the determiner slot and nothing else, so rule 49 leaves the article whatever other English the ASV supplies for it. The anarthrous ἕκαστος → every one at 18:35 is the contrast and heads on the quantifier for exactly that reason.

The accepted unit cited rule 17's generic-noun clause, which that rule scopes in terms to anarthrous Greek and hands to rule 102 wherever a Greek article governs the phrase.
